title: Symmetrical OTA
description: The symmetrical (or 'fully symmetric mirror') OTA is the push-pull sibling of the current-mirror OTA. Instead of loading one input side, BOTH input drains feed diode-connected mirror loads; one branch mirrors (ratio $K_m$) to the top PMOS output device and the other mirrors through an intermediate stage to the bottom NMOS output device, so the two input branches recombine at a push-pull output. The consequence is symmetric slewing in both directions, SR = $K_m*I_{tail}/C_L$ up and down, and the balanced signal path improves systematic offset. The transconductance and gain math match the current-mirror OTA — GBW = $K_m*g_{m,in}/(2*\pi*C_L)$, gain nearly $K_m$-independent — but there are now two mirror-node poles (the top PMOS and the intermediate NMOS mirror), both estimate-grade; sim owns settling.

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the output mirror devices' vds

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.89-1.42 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. The max must stay below the diode-loaded drain (VDD minus the mirror's |vgs|) — both bracket ends have to size

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: K_m
params.note: mirror ratio: multiplies GBW and both-direction slew, but raises input noise as sqrt(K_m) at fixed GBW

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise floor

params.name: gm_id_ml
params.note: mirror (diode) inversion, both the PMOS input mirror and the intermediate NMOS mirror

params.name: gm_id_mo
params.note: output-device inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher output resistance

doc.title: Input mirror device (PMOS diode)
doc.description: One of the two symmetric diode-connected PMOS loads at half the tail current; mirrors ratio K_m to the top output device. Its gate node carries a mirror pole.

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current, driving one of the two symmetric diode mirror loads. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain one diode drop below the supply, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the two.

doc.title: Top output device (PMOS)
doc.description: The K_m-scaled top output copy sourcing K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is one half of the output conductance.

doc.title: Intermediate mirror device (NMOS diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected second-path mirror that folds the other input branch to the bottom output device; carries the K_m-scaled current and adds the second mirror pole. Diode-connected, so its drop is read off the vds = vgs diagonal rather than guessed.

doc.title: Bottom output device (NMOS)
doc.description: The K_m-scaled bottom output copy sinking K_m times the input-branch current; its gds is the other half of the output conductance.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: Gm_out
rows.note: output transconductance = mirror ratio times the input gm

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: push-pull output node loaded by both output devices' conductance

rows.name: Av
rows.note: DC gain, nearly K_m-independent (K_m scales Gm_out and the output conductance together)

rows.name: SR
rows.note: symmetric slew: the push-pull output sources and sinks K_m*I_tail equally

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the mirror load's own density referred by gm_mloadp/gm_in

rows.name: f_pole_p
rows.note: estimate: the PMOS mirror-node pole (diode gm over its own plus the K_m-scaled output gate cap)

rows.name: f_pole_n
rows.note: estimate: the intermediate NMOS mirror-node pole — the diode gm over its own plus the output device's gate cap, mirroring f_pole_p's accounting

rows.name: PM
rows.note: estimate: the two mirror nodes cost phase differently, because the signal reaches them differently. Both input branches pass the PMOS mirror, so $f_{pole,p}$ is a full pole. Only the branch heading for the bottom output passes the intermediate NMOS mirror, so half the signal is delayed there and $f_{pole,n}$ is a pole-ZERO DOUBLET — a zero at twice the pole — costing far less phase than the pole alone implies. Measured against the ACHIEVED GBW

rules.note: estimate: margin left at crossover once both mirror nodes are paid for; advisory, since an open-loop OTA needs none of it and sim owns the real stability
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the diode load — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less diode drop
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges prove the range ENDS close, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, its own devices — and every hard rule must hold there

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way. Edges prove the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
